MV Linden Star

MV Linden Star
OperatorHarbor City Transit
BuilderOkafor & Sons, Riverside
Launched1998
Capacity240 passengers

The MV Linden Star is a passenger ferry operated by Harbor City Transit on the Pier 3 to Linden Street route. Built in 1998, she is the oldest vessel in the fleet still in daily service, and she was chosen in 2026 to run the city’s night ferry pilot.[1]

The ferry was refitted in 2015, when her diesel engines were replaced with quieter units and a covered upper deck was added. Crews have nicknamed her "the Lantern" because of the row of amber lights along her rail, which were installed after a near miss in fog.

History[edit]

The Linden Star was ordered in 1996, together with a sister ship that was later sold to an island operator. She entered service in the spring of 1998, and for most of her career she ran the busy commuter crossing during the morning and evening peaks.

Night service

In October 2026 the city council approved a six-month pilot of overnight sailings, and the Linden Star was assigned to the route because her refitted engines are the quietest in the fleet. Residents near the piers had raised concerns about noise during the debate.[2]
